entities.name: Johannes von Baysen
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Johannes von Baysen (c. 1398–1459), known also by his Polish name Jan Bażyński, emerged as a pivotal figure in 15th-century Central European history, orchestrating the dramatic shift of Prussia from the dominion of the Teutonic Order to a semi-autonomous province under the Polish Crown. As the charismatic leader of the Prussian Confederation and later the first Polish governor of Royal Prussia, Baysen's political acumen and military leadership were instrumental in precipitating the Thirteen Years' War (1454–1466) and fundamentally redrawing the geopolitical map of the southern Baltic region.

Baysen, a knight from a prominent Prussian noble family, initially served the Teutonic Order but became disillusioned with its oppressive rule, heavy taxation, and infringement on the traditional rights of the Prussian estates (nobility and burghers). He became a leading voice in the anti-Teutonic movement, co-founding the Prussian Confederation in 1440, an alliance of cities and nobles dedicated to resisting the Order's authority. In 1454, Baysen led the Confederation in formally requesting incorporation into the Kingdom of Poland, an act that triggered the Thirteen Years' War. He played a crucial role in securing Polish military support and subsequently organized the administration of the newly formed Royal Prussia, personally commanding forces and navigating complex political allegiances throughout the protracted conflict.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Johannes von Baysen was a central figure in the reorientation of Prussia from the Teutonic Order's control to the Polish Crown, directly leading to the formation of Royal Prussia and shifting the balance of power in the Baltic region for centuries.
